## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Tutorial packaging format and versioning scheme

## Description

Defines the tutorial packaging format — the structure every curated tutorial is
published in — so that tutorials are versioned and testable independently of
Dashboard releases. The format covers tutorial metadata, pinned images, and a
validation manifest. It is the shared contract consumed by the Dashboard
tutorial gallery (to render and launch tutorials) and by tutorial authors (to
package and validate content).

## Scope

- Define the tutorial packaging format with the three elements the strategy
  names: tutorial metadata, pinned images (the workbench and pipeline images a
  tutorial runs on), and a validation manifest describing how the tutorial is
  tested.
- Define the versioning model: a packaged tutorial declares the release it
  targets and carries its own version, independent of Dashboard releases.
- Define how a validation manifest is executed against a pinned release, so
  tutorial testing does not require a Dashboard build. The per-tutorial
  validation runs themselves are performed by the tutorial-authoring work, not
  here.
- Produce a minimal reference package that conforms to the format and passes
  its validation checks, demonstrating the contract end to end.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The packaging format specification defines all three stated elements —
  metadata, pinned images, validation manifest — such that a tutorial can be
  packaged by following the spec alone.
- A tutorial packaged per the format is versioned and testable independently of
  Dashboard releases: the package declares its target release, and its
  validation manifest can be executed without a Dashboard build.
- The reference package validates successfully against the format's validation
  checks.
- The format as delivered is sufficient for the Dashboard gallery launch
  mechanics (rendering a gallery entry and launching a tutorial from its
  metadata and pinned image) and for packaging both notebook and pipeline
  tutorials, with no format changes required after handoff.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): a tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation
  manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of
  Dashboard releases. This epic is P0 by priority inheritance: the format is
  the contract that both the Dashboard gallery (HLR-1) and the curated
  tutorials (HLR-2) build against, so it gates all P0 work in this strategy.
  HLR-3's P1 label reflects sequencing, not deferrability — the format cannot
  ship after the content that depends on it.

# Dashboard tutorial gallery and one-click launch

## Description

Adds the tutorial gallery to the Dashboard: a curated, browsable set of
tutorials that a user can launch into their own project with one click —
opening a workbench with the tutorial notebook loaded, or importing the
tutorial pipeline into the project.

## Scope

- Gallery surface in the Dashboard listing the curated tutorials with the
  metadata carried by the tutorial packaging format.
- One-click launch for notebook tutorials: opens a workbench in the user's
  project with the tutorial notebook, using the image pinned in the tutorial
  package.
- One-click launch for pipeline tutorials: imports the packaged pipeline into
  the user's project.
- Launch mechanics operate through the existing Kubernetes CR surfaces the
  Dashboard already manages for workbenches and pipelines.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can open the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard and see the curated
  tutorials with their packaged metadata.
- One-click launch of a notebook tutorial opens a workbench in the user's
  project with the tutorial notebook loaded, running the image pinned in the
  tutorial package.
- One-click launch of a pipeline tutorial imports the pipeline into the user's
  project.
- Launch behavior is verified using a tutorial package conformant with the
  tutorial packaging format, for both launch modes (workbench opening and
  pipeline import).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): the Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch
  a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or
  importing the pipeline).

# Notebook tutorial suite for the core journeys

## Description

Authors the notebook-based curated tutorials covering the core onboarding
journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first deployment, and
first RAG app. Each tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format and
tested against the current release.

## Scope

- Author five notebook tutorials covering: first workbench, data prep, first
  training run, first deployment, first RAG app.
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned
  images, validation manifest).
- Execute each tutorial's validation manifest against the current release and
  fix failures until every tutorial passes.
- Run tutorials on standard workbench images pinned via the packaging format.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Five notebook tutorials exist covering the five journeys listed in Scope.
- Each tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format with metadata,
  pinned images, and a validation manifest.
- Each tutorial passes its validation manifest when run against the current
  release — tested, not merely authored.
- Each packaged tutorial is format-conformant such that it can be surfaced and
  launched by the Dashboard's gallery launch mechanics without repackaging.

  (first workbench, data prep, first training run, first deployment, first RAG
  app), each tested against the current release. The remaining journey (first
  pipeline) is a pipeline artifact covered by the pipeline-tutorial work under
  the Data Science Pipelines component and its owning team.

# Tutorial gallery usage and contribution documentation

## Description

Documents the tutorial gallery for two audiences: end users learning to use
the gallery, and contributors authoring new curated tutorials. Published
through the Red Hat docs content process.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Using the gallery: what the tutorial gallery is; browsing the curated
  tutorials; launching a tutorial into your own project in both modes (opening
  a workbench with the notebook, and importing the pipeline); what to expect
  from a launched tutorial.
- Contributing tutorials: the contribution process for new tutorials —
  packaging a tutorial per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned
  images, validation manifest), the validation requirements a tutorial must
  pass against the current release, and how a tutorial becomes curated.
  Community/partner submission tooling is out of scope for this release and is
  not documented as available functionality.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covering using the gallery (browsing tutorials; launching
  notebook and pipeline tutorials into a project) is published.
- Documentation covering the contribution process for new tutorials is
  published, consistent with the tutorial packaging format and its validation
  requirements.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented gallery
  and the packaged tutorials.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution
  process for new tutorials.

Data Science Pipelines, Documentation). Not docs-only: the Dashboard gallery is
